name: HARLEY-DAVIDSON INC HOG
description: Description Introduction: Harley-Davidson, Inc. (“Harley”, “HOG” or the “Company”) was recently written up on VIC as a short by ElmSt14.  While we are in agreement with many of the points raised by the author, we have taken the opposite view in terms of valuation.  At the recent share price of $17.19, investors have the unique opportunity to purchase an American icon at a rock bottom valuation.  Harley currently has a market capitalization of under $1.9 billion and an enterprise value of $934 million after excluding non-recourse debt that is consolidated from Harley-Davidson Financial Services (HDFS).  Harley also expects to receive an additional ~$250 million dividend from HDFS in Q1 2026 which should take the Company’s adjusted enterprise value of under $700 million.  Additionally, Harley’s new CEO is reversing the destructive policies implemented by his predecessor which should lead to a dramatic improvement in Harley’s operating performance.  We see upside of well over 100% with minimal downside and recently made Harley-Davidson one of our largest positions.  Investment Thesis: Home Depot Relative ValuationWalmart Relative ValuationCVS Relative ValuationGoldman Sachs Relative ValuationMorgan Stanley Relative ValuationCaterpillar Relative ValuationDeere Relative ValuationHilton Relative ValuationYum Brands Relative ValuationFedex Relative Valuation After deconsolidating the balance sheet, Harley-Davidson’s enterprise value is much lower than what is indicated by most financial websites and sell-side analysts with Harley having an enterprise value of under $950 million. While criticized by many analysts, HDFS’s recent sale of $6.0 billion in consumer loans generated significant excess cash that has been utilized to reduce debt, repurchase shares, and build a net cash balance over $1 billion.  New CEO Artie Starrs has acted decisively to reverse the destructive policies implemented by his predecessor and recently made a $286,500 insider purchase of Harley stock.  Harley’s majority ownership of Livewire, an electric motorcycle company, is likely to be wound down in the next year with minimal additional financial impact on Harley.  Valuation is extremely attractive.  Treating the parent company as a standalone entity reveals a rock-solid balance sheet with $1.0bn in net cash and 90.2% equity ownership in HDFS.  The Harley-Davidson Motor Company has historically generated over $4.0bn in sales and $250-$700 million in EBITDA.     Current Valuation after Deconstructing the Balance Sheet: Harley’s consolidated financial statements suggest the Company has a good balance sheet including $3.1 billion of cash and $3.0 billion of debt for a net cash balance of ~$100 million.  Importantly, many investors appear to be overlooking the fact that Harley is now a majority holder of HDFS (90.2% equity stake), and the vast majority of Harley’s consolidated debt is held at HDFS which has $1.8 billion of cash and $2.7 billion of debt (all non-recourse to Harley).  Deconsolidating HDFS and LiveWire from Harley’s consolidated financial statements highlights the true financial strength of the company.  Harley helps investors out by deconsolidating their income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statements on pages 119-130 from the Company’s 10-K.  Our analysis below also deconsolidates Harley’s equity stake in LiveWire to highlight the enterprise value of HDMC before and after the Q1 2026 dividend from HDFS.  The deconsolidation reveals that the Harley-Davidson Motor Company (HDMC) has $1.2 billion of cash and just $300 million of debt, resulting in a net cash balance of over $900 million and an enterprise value for Harley-Davidson of under $934 million.  Additionally, Harley has highlighted that HDFS has $264 million of receivables left to be sold to KKR and PIMCO.  HDFS is expected to dividend an additional ~$250 million to HDMC in Q1 2026 once the receivables sale takes place.  Pro-forma for the additional ~$250 million dividend from HDFS, and Harley has over $1.15 billion in net cash (over 60% of the Company’s market cap) and an Enterprise value of just $684 million.  Harley has repurchased a significant amount of stock in recent months (including 3.15 million shares of stock after year-end), and we expect the Company could aggressively repurchase stock with its sizeable cash balance following Harley’s Investor Day in May.    Harley-Davidson Financial Services Transaction: In July 2025, Harley-Davidson Financial Services (HDFS) announced a transaction with KKR and PIMCO.  The transaction is complicated, but our main takeaways are below:  KKR and PIMCO will purchase around $6 billion of HDFS’s retail loan book at a premium to par. KKR and PIMCO can purchase 2/3 of future retail loans originated by HDFS over the next 5 years. KKR and PIMCO will each purchase 4.9% of HDFS equity.
